newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended weak in active trade, with the industrial and all-share indices shedding over 100 points on negative sentiment. Gold shares eased in sympathy.
"It was a very weak market. The Dow is down, the rand is weak and the futures close-out is approaching on Tuesday. Sentiment is just not right," one dealer said.
The market was knocked by the Dow Jones' 98.81 points slide on Thursday night to 6,303.7 points.
Dealers said the local market was jittery in line with world markets. Blue chip stocks were the hardest hit, they said.
The U.S. futures market was weak which could mean further Wall Street losses, dealers said and saw the Dow Jones index supported at 6,200.
The market ended off lows and players squared positions ahead of the long weekend, dealers said. Monday is the Day of Reconciliation public and market holiday in South Africa.
The bullion price has been hovering around the $369 an ounce level, dulling interest in gold shares. Gold shares were largely ignored despite a stronger rand gold price.
"Golds were dissapointing. The higher rand gold price on the weaker rand did not help them," one dealer said.
The industrial index fell 132.2 points to 7,682.5 points, the all share index lost 124.5 points to 6,482.5 points and the gold index dropped 21.6 points to 1,511.6 points.

Near-term industrial index futures ended weak in nearvous trade on Wall Street's losses overnight. Dealers said players were selling the underlying stock and buying the future which pushed the cash market lower.

They said players were reluctant to take positions over the long weekend as Wall Street seemed volatile. "The guys are reluctant to take positions ahead of the weekend. They don't want to have to sit through Friday and Monday," a dealer said.
Golds contracts also ended weak, ignoring a better rand gold price.
The December all-share contract was last bid at 5,800 form Thursday's 5,998 settlement, the industrial contract was last at 7,310/24 from 7,502 and the gold index was at 1,045/55 from 1,068.
De Beers lost 325 cents to 134.25 rand, First National dropped 6.21 percent to 20.40 rand, Malbak was 5.21 percent weaker at 20 rand and Freegold shed 3.10 percent to 34.40 rand.
